newsitem.title: CANADA: Videotron protests Pacific Telesis action.
newsitem.headline: Videotron protests Pacific Telesis action.

text.p: Groupe Videotron Ltee said on Wednesday it is contesting a decision by Pacific Telesis Group to terminate the proposed $170 million purchase of its wireless cable interests (MMDS) in the U.S.

Videotron said that the purchase agreement had a provision for termination by any of the parties after November 9 if closing had not occurred, providing the terminating party had complied with all of its obligations under the agreement.
Videotron said the companies had already engaged in an arbitration proceeding in which Videotron is contesting Pacific Telesis' right to exercise the termination provision.

Under the purchase agreement, Pacific Telesis agreed to buy all the stock of Wireless Holdings Inc (WHI) and Videotron (BAy Area) Inc (VBAI), which own wireless cable rights and certain operating wireless cables systems in various West Coast cities and in Tampa, Florida and Greenville, South Carolina, Videotron said.

Videotron indirectly owns 50 percent of WHI and 80 percent of VBAI and holds indebtedness of the two companies aggregating $50 million. Videtron had anticipated receiving more than $110 million as its share of the proceeds of the proposed sale, the company said.
